headline: Trump at final midterm rally in Salina, Kansas
dek: Trump told his 30th and final midterm rally in Salina, Kansas that Washington has 'dominated' Iran and 'we can close them down anytime we want'; 'We're trying to be nice... it's going to be very close.
sources: Donald Trump, Salina (Kansas) midterm rally, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Deal now vs 'close them down': is the Salina line a final pre-midterm warning or campaign rhetoric that collapses after the vote?

sections.what_happened: Trump told his 30th and final midterm rally in Salina, Kansas that Washington has 'dominated' Iran and 'we can close them down anytime we want'; 'We're trying to be nice... it's going to be very close. We're just going to close them down. That's going to be the end of it.' Distinct rally/quote from the Iowa 'hammer' quote already recorded in 0600-03 (same threat line, new venue and wording).
sections.what_verified: AJ liveblog relay of the Salina rally speech.
sections.what_disputed: Same speech also says the US is 'trying to be nice' and has not decided on strikes (Rubio, recorded 0600-01); Doha two-day Hormuz plan still awaits a US response (0800-01). Threat rhetoric is not a strike decision.
sections.why_matters: Trump's LAST rally before the midterms: 'we can close them down anytime' — the threat line, sharpened, 1-2 days from the reported decision window.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 04:30 GMT = 08:30 ) -- Trump at final midterm rally in Salina, Kansas: US can 'close down' Iran 'anytime we want'

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump's LAST rally before the midterms: 'we can close them down anytime' — the threat line, sharpened, 1-2 days from the reported decision window. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deal now vs 'close them down': is the Salina line a final pre-midterm warning or campaign rhetoric that collapses after the vote?
